name: Week 19 Legs — Steady State, Station-Grouped (Spotlight: Squat Depth + Leg Curl)
description: Volume steady, station-grouped. **Warmup reminder:** bodyweight squat (depth check) → cross-leg lateral lean (QL/psoas) → hip circles → tibialis raise → cat-cow → internal core fist rotation → dead-bug core/QL primer (the W19 test) → bodyweight lunge (QL check). Spotlights cycle forward to the squat (depth refresh — your own 45→70→80 ROM-building ramp, formalized) and the leg curl (form-first at 80, the 70 primer grooving the pattern). Squat holds 80/side with depth as the lever, not heavier weight. Bulgarian holds double-45 DBs (Smith @45 the confirmed QL-safe alternate), with pigeon-on-the-bench between sets as a station option (your W18 keeper). Leg curl at 80 working; incline RDL holds the dead-slow 45lb-plate hinge. The dead-bug primer is the test of whether waking the core early changes the leg press.

dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Spotlights cycle to squat depth (formalize the 45→70→80 ROM ramp — depth is the lever) + leg curl (form-first at 80, 70 primer grooves the pattern). Squat holds 80, depth the focus. Bulgarian double-45 DB default / Smith @45 alternate, pigeon between sets. New this week: a dead-bug core/QL primer in the warmup — the test of whether waking the core early settles the leg press (after W18's 'sweating like a wet dog' session). Leg curl stays before incline RDL so the hamstring work doesn't stack.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward as the depth refresh — W18 you restructured the block yourself around ROM: a 70 intermediary set then 80x6/80x8, ROM 'better than last week, ~85%,' stated goal 'fix the ROM + the mid-range; hips still super tight.' Spotlight formalizes that 45→70→80 ramp and makes depth the explicit lever — chase the bottom set by set, hold 80, don't push load.

Cycles forward — W18 you dropped to 80 working (from 90) on purpose: the 70 primer 'primes my brain to do it correctly' and 80 'feels pretty correct vs what it used to be.' Spotlight drills that correct feel at 80 (form-first, not a regression) so the pattern grooves — 90 returns only once 80 is automatic, not before.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W17 squat depth + incline RDL · W18 leg-press ROM + Bulgarian · W19 squat depth + leg curl (current) · W20 cycle forward — leg press + Bulgarian refresh.
watchpoints: **Loads** — squat 80/side (depth-gated working sets off the 45→70→80 ramp), leg press 4 plates (ROM first), calf raise 4 plates, leg curl 80 working (5/m/0/-1, 70 primer), incline RDL 45lb plate, Bulgarian double-45 DBs (Smith @45 the alternate).

**Squat spotlight — the 45→70→80 ROM ramp, depth is the lever.** 45x8 to drill max depth, 70x6-8 as the ROM intermediary, then 80 working — chase the bottom every set ('better ROM than last week, ~85%'). Reps are NOT the point right now; ROM + the mid-range are. Run 80 for as many working sets as depth holds; stop adding sets when the depth shortens. Hips still super tight — keep breathing into the bottom.

**Leg curl spotlight — form-first at 80.** Settings 5/m/0/-1 (verify before loading). First set at 70 to groove the pattern ('primes my brain to do it correctly'), then 80 working with the slow eccentric. 80 done correctly beats 90 with drift — let 90 return only once 80 is automatic. Don't push back to 90.

**Dead-bug core/QL primer in the warmup — the W19 test.** W18's leg press was unusually brutal ('sweating like a wet dog') with the core/QL pre-fatigued from Thursday's figure-8s; your read was 'should do more to wake it up.' This week a short dead-bug set wakes the deep core before the leg press — watch whether the leg press feels more normal when the QL ISN'T pre-fatigued from Thursday. It's a test, not a fix.

**Bulgarian → double-45 DBs (regular DB is the DEFAULT).** The Smith machine is the SWAP-IN when it's free — it's cleared the QL test at 45/side two weeks running (W17 + W18). **Pigeon on the bench between sets** kept the hip/QL loose W18 ('really helped') — use it as a station option. If anything twitches, drop to bodyweight and finish.
**Leg press ROM** — deep knees-to-chest, lower back stays on the pad. It feels harder cold and opens by the end; don't judge the load on set 1. Hold 4 plates, ROM-first.
**Station-grouped sequence:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (SAME machine, stay there) → Bulgarian (bench station) → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — reversed, the two hamstring lifts stack and smoke the second.

**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. QL's been clear (W18 'sore but no spasms' even going in tight from Thursday's figure-8s). If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set + take stretch breaks (your self-regulation W18 worked).

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release + Dead-Bug Core/QL Primer)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.

Back to a wall, heels a step out, weight on the heels. Pull the toes UP toward the shins as high as they'll go, lower slow. Wakes the shins (the calf's antagonist), preps ankle dorsiflexion for squat depth, and it's shin insurance for the run-in. ~30s, bodyweight.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain and low-back opener before loading the squat.

**Core/QL primer — the W19 test.** On your back, arms up, knees over hips. Press the lower back FLAT into the floor and HOLD it there as you slowly extend the opposite arm + leg, then switch. The brace is the work — wakes the deep core before the leg press. (W18 the leg press ran brutal with the core pre-fatigued; this is the test of whether waking it early changes that — watch how the leg press feels today.)
Bodyweight. QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian pattern.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT (depth refresh) — the bottom half of your 45→70→80 ramp:**
- **Set 1: 45/side x8** — used to DRILL max depth. Depth isn't 100% even here, so chase it light: sit all the way into the bottom, breathe, feel where the hips block.
- **Set 2: 70/side x6** — the intermediary ROM-builder (your W18 self-found tool). Same depth as the working sets, heavier than the 45 so the bottom is honest. This is where the mid-range gets drilled before 80.

**LOAD:** 80/side. Working sets off the ramp — run 80 for 6-8 reps, as many sets as your depth holds (W18 was 80x6 then 80x8, ROM '~85%, better than last week'). **Depth is the lever, not reps or load** — your stated goal is fixing the ROM + the mid-range; hips still super tight.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — chase the bottom set by set:**
- Bar high on the upper traps (NOT the neck), upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, not just down
- **'Spread the floor'** — screw the feet in, knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — keep chasing depth; you find depth easier under load, so trust the 80 to help you sink
- Drive through the WHOLE foot
- **Stop adding working sets when the depth shortens** — a shallow grind isn't the work; bank the deep ones

**Reflection:** does the bottom get deeper as you warm through the ramp (45 → 70 → 80), and does 80 hold ~85%+ depth — or does it shorten under load? Deep at 80 is the win; if depth caps, that's the honest end, hold 80 and keep drilling the ramp.

sets.name: Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — Leg Press ROM)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 4 sets of 12.
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest.** The deep position trains the abs/QL/core as much as the quads — that's the intent ('legs barely doing anything in the deep squat')
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out
- **It feels harder cold** — the deep ROM opens up once the hips are warm, so don't judge the load on set 1
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom; if the hips roll off, back off a hair (or stop just shy of the catcher)
- **Press through the WHOLE foot** — heels grounded
- **Slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**; don't lock out hard at the top
- **Note for the test:** W18 this ran unusually brutal ('sweating like a wet dog') with the core pre-fatigued. With the dead-bug primer + a clear QL today, see if it feels more normal. Hold 4 plates, ROM-first — don't read one hard session as a load change.

**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off.
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **Tempo by feel** — own the stretch at the bottom and the squeeze at the top, no bouncing. (3 sets, after the 4 leg-press sets — same station.)

sets.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Double-45 DBs — Smith @45 the Alternate; Pigeon Between Sets)

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs (regular default) — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** two 45lb DBs, one per hand. 3 sets of 8-10 each leg. **Regular DB version is the default; the Smith machine is the swap-in when it's free** (it's cleared the QL test at 45/side two weeks — W17 + W18 — so it's a confirmed QL-safe alternate).

**Pigeon on the bench between sets** — W18 keeper ('really helped' keep the hip/QL loose under the split-squat load). Take it between sets, plus stretch breaks as needed.
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over
- **2s descent**, own the bottom

**Watch:** at double-45 this is real load — if anything twitches/spasms, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish.

sets.name: 🔆 Seated Leg Curl (Spotlight — 5/m/0/-1, 70 Primer + 80 Working, Before Incline RDL)

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 70 first set to center, then 80 working. Slow tempo. **Settings: 5/m/0/-1** (verify before loading — the setting that felt better than /1 in W17).

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — the correct feel at 80, form-first:**
- **First set at 70 to groove the pattern** — 'primes my brain to do it correctly' (it'll feel easy; that's the point)
- **Then 80 for the working sets** — W18 this 'felt pretty correct vs what it used to be.' 80 done right beats 90 with drift; let 90 return only once 80 is automatic — don't push back to 90
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze
- **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — the slow eccentric is the whole stimulus; you feel these deeply when you go slow
- Torso anchored, no lifting forward. This comes BEFORE incline RDL on purpose — take the working sets with the legs still relatively fresh.

**Reflection:** does 80 keep that 'correct' feel (heels driving, hamstring doing the work, no torso lift) for all the working sets — or does it start drifting? The correct feel IS the win here, not the number. When 80 is automatic, 90 comes back on its own.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom. (W18 the slow squeeze was dialing in — hitting the hamstrings/glutes so well it was 'hard to get off the machine'; that's the form landing.)
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**; at the top, stop at neutral — past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** The slow eccentric is the entire reason this works — hold the 45lb plate, keep slowing the tempo; don't chase the load. (If the legs are smoked from the leg press, cutting the last set is the honest end, not a regression.)

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

tips: **Steady state, station-grouped.** Squat ramp (45/70 + 80 working), leg press 4, calf raise 3, Bulgarian 3, leg curl 3, incline RDL 3.
**Spotlight: squat depth + leg curl.** Squat formalizes your 45→70→80 ROM ramp (depth the lever, not load); leg curl drills the correct feel at 80 (form-first, 70 primer grooves it).
**Squat holds 80 — depth is the work.** Chase the bottom each set; stop adding working sets when depth shortens. Hips still tight — breathe into the bottom.
**Leg curl 80 working, not 90** — 80 done correctly beats 90 with drift. Let 90 return only once 80 is automatic.
**Dead-bug core/QL primer in the warmup — the W19 test.** Wakes the core before the leg press; watch whether the leg press normalizes with the QL not pre-fatigued from Thursday.
**Bulgarian double-45 DBs, regular version is the default.** Smith @45 is the confirmed QL-safe alternate (2 weeks clear). Pigeon on the bench between sets ('really helped' W18).
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them, or the hamstring work stacks.
**Incline RDL is a 45lb plate, dead slow** — tempo is the progression; the slow squeeze is dialing in.
**Cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down** — QL/psoas release. QL held W18 even going in tight; keep bookending it + take stretch breaks.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.**
Rest: 3 min squats, 2 min leg press, 90s calf raise + Bulgarian + isolations.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state legs week. The squat and leg curl get the deep-cue treatment — both around quality, not load: the squat formalizes the user's own 45→70→80 ROM-building ramp with depth as the explicit lever (goal = fix the ROM + the mid-range), and the leg curl drills the correct feel at 80 (the 70 primer grooves the pattern; 90 returns only once 80 is automatic). A dead-bug core/QL primer joins the warmup to test the user's instinct that the core is the exposed weak link. The sequence keeps the two hamstring lifts from stacking and the station order from backtracking. Form leads load — building decades, not weeks.
